Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be marked on your ability to use good English to organize information clearly and to use specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the main function of the following in an intranet:

(a) Firewall. (2 marks)

(b) Switch. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Firewall (2 marks)**

A firewall is a hardware device or a program placed **between the intranet and the outside network (the Internet)**. It examines all the data entering and leaving the intranet and applies a set of rules to **block unauthorised traffic and intruders** and to allow only permitted traffic, so it protects the organisation's data and computers from hackers and malicious programs.

**(b) Switch (2 marks)**

A switch is the device to which the computers of the intranet (LAN) are connected. It **receives the data frames and forwards each one only to the port of the destination computer** (it learns the addresses of the connected computers), instead of broadcasting it to all of them like a hub. This reduces collisions and traffic, and increases the speed and the security of the network.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An outsourcing software has been produced for your organization.

(a) Give THREE areas you will use to investigate the effectiveness of the software. (3 marks)

(b) Give TWO importance of outsourcing. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three areas to investigate the effectiveness of the software (3 marks)**

- **Meeting the user requirements**: does the software do all the tasks specified by the organisation, and does it produce the correct and expected outputs?
- **Ease of use**: are the screens, menus and reports easy for the staff to use, and what do the users say (a questionnaire or an interview), how much training is needed?
- **Performance and reliability**: speed of processing, accuracy of the results, number of errors or breakdowns, and security of the data.
- (Other valid areas: compatibility with the existing hardware and software; the cost compared with the benefits; the quality of the documentation and of the technical support.)

**(b) Two importance (advantages) of outsourcing (2 marks)**

- The organisation obtains the **skills and experience of specialists** that it does not have in its own staff, so the quality of the software is usually higher.
- It **saves cost and time**: the organisation does not need to recruit and train a permanent team or to buy development equipment, and it can **concentrate on its core business**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the function of the following in computer system:

(a) BIOS. (2 marks)

(b) Sound Card. (2 marks)

(c) Cache Memory. (2 marks)

(d) Motherboard. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) BIOS (2 marks)**

The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is a small program stored in a ROM or flash memory chip on the motherboard. When the computer is switched on it runs the **power-on self-test (POST)** to check the hardware, and then **finds the operating system on the disk and loads it into RAM** (the bootstrap). It also provides the basic routines for communicating with the keyboard, the disks and the other devices, and stores the hardware settings.

**(b) Sound card (2 marks)**

The sound card (an expansion card or a chip on the motherboard) **converts the digital sound data of the computer into analogue signals** that are sent to the loudspeakers or headphones, and **converts the analogue sound from a microphone into digital data** that the computer can store and process.

**(c) Cache memory (2 marks)**

The cache is a **small and very fast memory** placed between the processor and the main memory (RAM). It stores **copies of the instructions and data that are used most often**, so that the CPU finds them quickly and does not have to wait for the slower RAM. This increases the speed of the computer.

**(d) Motherboard (2 marks)**

The motherboard is the **main circuit board** of the computer. It holds the processor, the RAM, the chipset, the BIOS chip and the expansion slots, and it **connects all the components together through the buses** so that they can exchange data; it also distributes the power to them.
